articles.title: Man charged with shooting SWAT officer and woman during hostage situation in Albany Park
articles.description:
A man was charged with shooting a SWAT officer and a woman during a standoff Monday in Albany Park on the Northwest Side.

Daniel Aguirre, 42, faced several felony charges including attempted murder, aggravated discharge of a firearm, aggravated battery, aggravated unlawful restraint, aggravated assault of a peace officer and aggravated discharge of a firearm in an occupied building, Chicago police said

He was arrested hours after the incident began Monday morning in the 4600 block of North Springfield Avenue, officials said.

Police responded around 11 a.m. to a call of a female shot in the 4600 block of North Springfield Avenue, interim Chicago police Supt. Fred Waller told reporters Monday afternoon. An internal police report indicated she had been shot in the face.

When SWAT officers tried to enter the home, the suspect fired through a door and struck one of the officers in the lower abdomen, according to Waller.

Aguirre was scheduled to appear in court Wednesday.

articles.title: Boy, 15, found fatally shot in Austin
articles.description:
A 15-year-old boy was found fatally shot early Wednesday in Austin on the West Side.

Just after 1 a.m., officers and paramedics responded to a call of a person shot in the 4600 block of West Jackson Boulevard and the boy was found shot in the head, Chicago police said.

He was taken to Stroger Hospital where he was pronounced dead, police said.

Area 4 detectives were investigating.

articles.title: Lack of defibrillators could put 16m at risk of death by cardiac arrest in England and Wales
articles.description: Exclusive: Research shows millions live more than a 1km round trip from 24/7 accessible device More than 16 million people in England and Wales risk dying from a cardiac arrest because they live farther than a 1km round trip from the nearest 24/7 defibrillator, according to exclusive research. Analysis of publicly available defibrillators by the Heart Restart campaign found that in England and Wales alone, 35 million people – more than half the population – do not live within the recommended three- to five-minute brisk walk of a defibrillator. Of these, about half live more than a 1km round trip from a 24/7 accessible defibrillator. There are more than 40,000 out-of-hospital cardiac arrests each year in the UK, but fewer than one in 10 people survive. However, early cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) and defibrillation can more than double the chance of survival. Continue reading...
